narration: This is the AI Government Benefits Navigator: an AI-powered assistant that helps citizens discover, understand, and access government welfare schemes.
It covers ten benefit categories, including education, agriculture, healthcare, and housing, all backed by a verified, structured scheme database that the AI never invents on its own.
Let's ask it a question the way a real user would, in plain natural language.
I am a twenty year old engineering student from Tamil Nadu. My family income is around one point five lakh rupees per year. What scholarships can I apply for?
The assistant extracts a structured profile, including age, state, student status, and income, using a dedicated extraction step, not a guess.

It retrieves candidate schemes from the verified database and runs each one through a transparent eligibility engine, with no arbitrary confidence scores, just clear matched, missing, and failed conditions.
Every recommendation explains exactly why it was suggested, and what information is still missing, right inside the card.
It also produces a clear document checklist, distinguishing required documents from possibly required ones.
The full scheme page shows the complete eligibility breakdown, step by step application instructions, and a direct link to the official government source.
Every scheme is clearly labeled with its source and last verified date. This particular dataset is sample data for the demo, and is never presented as real.
Users who prefer not to type free text can fill a short guided profile instead. No Aadhaar numbers, passwords, or bank details are ever requested.
The My Benefits dashboard tracks likely eligible, needs verification, and saved schemes at a glance, with clear recommended next steps.
Government benefits already exist. The problem is access. This tool bridges that gap with transparent, explainable, and multilingual guidance in English and Tamil.
